meta.subtitle: Double-digit growth and an 11.8x NTM multiple, with the shares near their 52-week low

analystSentiment.commentary:
Intuit's reported numbers and its share price tell opposite stories. FY26 delivered steady growth, a wider operating margin and a step-up in cash generation. Yet at $282.78 on October 1, 2026 the stock sits far below its 52-week high of $689.17 and close to the low of $252.84.

The filing does not explain the decline, and we have no news coverage in our data that does. That is the central uncertainty in this report: the market may be pricing a threat the reported numbers do not yet show. The 10-K's own risk factors describe the most likely candidates, which we weigh under Risks.

Our view is that the current price already discounts a great deal of that threat, given the forward multiple and the cash the business returns (see Valuation and Management).

We rate INTU BUY with a $290–$360 target range.

executiveSummary.companyOverview:
Intuit Inc. provides financial management, tax, payments and capital, and marketing products and services, mainly in the United States. Its brands include QuickBooks and Mailchimp for small and mid-market businesses, and TurboTax, Credit Karma and its professional tax software for consumers and tax preparers.

Effective August 1, 2025, the company combined its Consumer, Credit Karma and ProTax businesses into a single Consumer segment, alongside Global Business Solutions. Effective August 1, 2026 it began managing Mailchimp as a separate operating segment, and Mailchimp will be a separate reportable segment beginning in fiscal 2027. The company is headquartered in Mountain View, California.

thesis.label: BUY
thesis.body: We rate BUY on a simple path: the business keeps generating cash and delivering consensus earnings, and the market holds today's multiple, which carries the shares to our Base case. The scenario weighting and its asymmetry are set out in Valuation. If the feared erosion shows up in results or estimates, the bear case becomes the base case.

catalysts: Delivery against consensus FY27 revenue and earnings.
The first separate Mailchimp segment disclosure in fiscal 2027.
Any repurchases at the current share price.
risks: Government-provided tax software competing with TurboTax.
Fraud, security or privacy incidents on a platform holding financial data.
An unidentified driver behind the share-price decline.

income.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended July 31 (FY26 ended July 31, 2026).

financials.incomeCommentary:
FY26 revenue was $21.4B, up {+13.9%+} from $18.8B in FY25, the fourth straight year of double-digit growth. Operating income rose to $5.9B and operating margin widened to 27.4% from 26.1%. Diluted EPS was $16.46, up from $13.67.

The counter-case is in the same series: growth slowed from 15.6% in FY25 to 13.9% in FY26, and Q4'26 revenue grew 12.1%, below the full-year rate. Consensus expects a further slowdown in FY27 (see Growth). Margins are doing more of the work as top-line growth eases.

The FY26 results absorb a $293 million restructuring charge under the 2026 Plan, which management estimates will total approximately $315 million.

Quarterly results are highly seasonal because tax revenue concentrates from November through April. The Q4'26 operating margin of 10.9% therefore cannot be compared with the full-year margin.

balance.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended July 31 (FY26 ended July 31, 2026).

financials.balanceCommentary:
Cash and short-term investments rose to $4.7B at FY26 year-end from $2.9B. Total debt rose to $7.7B from $6.0B, leaving net debt roughly flat at $3.0B. The current ratio improved to 1.51 from 1.36.

Total equity fell to $19.0B from $19.7B in a year when buybacks and dividends together exceeded net income of $4.6B. Net debt is small relative to the year's cash generation, so the balance sheet does not constrain the company.

cashflow.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended July 31 (FY26 ended July 31, 2026).

financials.cashflowCommentary:
Operating cash flow rose to $8.8B from $6.2B, which management reports as up 42%. Capital expenditure was small at -$175M, so free cash flow reached $8.7B, a 40.4% FCF margin against 32.5% in FY25.

The jump in cash flow outpaced the rise in net income, so part of it may reflect working-capital timing; we would not extrapolate the full FY26 margin. Even at the FY25 margin, the business generates cash well beyond its dividend and capital spending.

multiples.note: Peer multiples pending a peer data source.

valuation.multiplesCommentary:
At $282.78 INTU trades at 17.2x trailing earnings, 11.8x NTM earnings, 10.4x FY28E EPS and 3.5x trailing sales, with a 2.00% dividend yield.

The Street remains positive but split: 34 analysts, 20 Buy, 12 Hold and 2 Sell. The consensus target is $405.60, implying +43.4%, with a median of $400.00 inside a wide range of $290.00–$732.00. The width of that range shows how far apart views on the disruption risk are.

We have no peer multiples to benchmark against, so we judge the forward multiple against growth instead: it is low for a business with the growth record described in Financials.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Consensus EPS of $23.94 for FY27E is met, the fear behind the decline fades, and the shares recover to a little above the consensus target of $405.60.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: The market keeps today's 11.8x NTM multiple and, a year from now, applies it to FY28E EPS of $27.08. The shares rise with earnings, with no re-rating.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: The feared erosion shows up: government or AI-enabled tax offerings take customers or pricing, estimates fall, and the shares break below both the 52-week low of $252.84 and the bottom of the Street target range.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
Base carries the most weight because it needs only consensus delivery at an unchanged multiple. Bull gets more weight than Bear because the cash the business generates supports the shares even if sentiment stays poor. Bear still carries a quarter of the weight because the cause of the decline is unknown and the risk factors describe credible ways the earnings base could erode.

The result is a weighted fair value of $321, an expected upside of +13.5% and a bear-case downside of -23.6%. The downside exceeds the expected upside, but the reward/risk still clears our BUY threshold.

Our $290–$360 target range brackets Base.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: Our sources disagree on segments. The vendor data carries one consolidated segment, and the company tearsheet describes an older four-segment structure. We use the FY26 10-K MD&A, which reports two segments: Global Business Solutions revenue of $12.9B, up 16%, and Consumer revenue of $8.6B, up 11%. Service offerings were $18.9 billion, or 88% of total revenue, and management expects that share to grow over the long term.

moatFactors.name: Recurring customer relationships
moatFactors.body: The 10-K says the tax businesses depend significantly on customers who return each year, and QuickBooks sits inside small businesses' daily accounting, payroll and payments. That recurrence underpins steady revenue. The same risk factor warns that retaining customers gets harder if they do not see continuing value.

moatFactors.name: Platform breadth and data
moatFactors.body: Intuit spans tax, accounting, payroll, payments, credit and marketing, and it uses consented customer data across the platform to build new offerings. Breadth raises switching costs. It also widens the surface for security, privacy and regulatory risk.

moatFactors.name: Funding capacity
moatFactors.body: The cash flow described in Financials lets Intuit fund AI development, product and marketing every year from operations. A startup competitor cannot match that budget. A large platform can, so this advantage protects against small entrants more than against large ones.

businessMoat.durability: We rate the moat NARROW. The page's quantitative screen reads it as wide, and today's margins and cash generation are consistent with that. We mark it narrower because the threats in Risks attack its two main supports: free and government tax offerings go at recurring tax customers, and AI-enabled rivals go at the value of platform breadth. The moat holds if Intuit's own AI investment keeps pace with new entrants.

points: Consensus expects FY27E revenue of $23.4B, up about 9%, and FY28E revenue of $25.6B. That is a slower path than FY26, so it leaves room for upside if growth holds near recent rates, and less room for error if it slows further.

The first separate Mailchimp disclosure, beginning in fiscal 2027, is worth watching: it will show whether that business is growing or diluting the rest of Global Business Solutions, which today we cannot see.

AI is the swing factor. The company is devoting significant resources to it but warns there is no assurance its AI innovations will be adopted or monetizable. In our view the test is simple: whether tax customers keep returning each season.

management.leadership: The captured proxy excerpt covers board independence and related-person policy but does not name the executive officers, so we do not comment on individual executives. The main management decision visible in the filing is the 2026 Plan, approved in May 2026, which the MD&A describes as simplifying the organizational structure to become a faster, leaner, more focused company. We discuss its execution risk under Risks.
management.capitalAllocation:
Intuit returned heavily to shareholders in FY26: share repurchases of -$5.4B, up from -$2.8B, and dividends of -$1.3B. Together they stayed within free cash flow.

The price paid for the FY26 repurchases, and their timing relative to the share-price decline, are not in our data. Any buyback at today's price would retire more shares per dollar, which is a reason to prefer repurchases over acquisitions while the shares stay depressed. The rise in total debt is covered in Financials.
management.governance: Per the proxy statement dated November 2025, the Board determined eleven directors and nominees independent under Nasdaq rules: Ms. Burton, Mr. Dalzell, Ms. Liu, Ms. Mawakana, Ms. Nora Johnson, Mr. Norrod, Mr. Prabhu, Mr. Roslansky, Mr. Szkutak, Mr. Vazquez and Mr. Yuan. Independent directors meet in closed session at each regularly scheduled meeting, and the Audit and Risk Committee pre-approves related-person transactions annually under a written policy. For a holder this means independent-majority oversight and a formal check on related-party dealings. The proxy also says the Board believes a balanced mix of board tenure is effective, which keeps long-serving directors whose independence from management needs watching. The excerpt carries no executive pay, insider ownership or related-person transaction amounts, so we cannot assess those. These facts predate the FY26 10-K and may have changed.

idiosyncratic: Government tax software: the 10-K warns that federal and state authorities could provide tax software at public expense. The IRS free direct filing system was suspended, but proponents continue to advocate for it, and the legacy IRS Free File Program could expand.

Free, low-cost and AI-enabled competition: the risk factors describe competitors ranging from startups to large platforms with established consumer user bases, and increasing free and low-cost competition in tax, accounting, payments and personal finance.

Fraud, security and privacy: Intuit holds customers' financial data in industries seeing increasingly sophisticated fraud, including AI-assisted fraud. A major incident would hit trust in the platform directly.

Reorganization execution: in our view, the workforce reductions and site closures under the 2026 Plan could disrupt product delivery or the retention of technical talent, which the MD&A says the growth strategy depends on.
risks.systemic: Intuit operates in a rapidly evolving regulatory environment with heightened scrutiny across tax, financial services, privacy and AI. Its small and mid-market business customers are exposed to the economic cycle, which affects QuickBooks, payments and lending activity. Seasonality concentrates tax revenue in a few months each year, so a disrupted filing season would weigh heavily on a single year's results.

body: BUY, target range $290–$360, on the case set out in the thesis and the scenario math in Valuation.

We would turn cautious if consensus estimates start to fall or if government or AI-enabled tax filing gains meaningful adoption. We would add conviction if FY27 results track the consensus path through the next tax season.
